For data analysis management, the system establishes a theoretical displacement model for communication towers based on national regulations, compares and analyzes the measured data from each monitoring point with the theoretical model, calculates parameters such as wind speed displacement, and automatically generates alarm information when measured displacement exceeds theoretical values. All monitoring data is stored on the server and generates statistical graphs such as displacement curves and wind speed statistical curves. For environmental monitoring management, the system monitors the environmental conditions within the base station micro-network through HDC1080 temperature and humidity sensors, which feature low power consumption and high accuracy, capable of simultaneously monitoring temperature and humidity data. The system automatically issues alarm signals when environmental indicators are abnormal. For early warning and alarm management, the system displays tower working status in text or graphical form, shows the operation status of each base station on maps through B/S network combined with GIS, uses different markers to identify abnormal conditions, promptly pushes fault information to maintenance personnel, and records the processing. Maintenance personnel have employee ID, name, contact information, and responsible area.

Record the basic information of players. Each player has a unique Player ID, which includes the player's username, password, game, phone number, and registration time. This table supports player identity authentication and basic information queries.

Record the basic information of the game. Each game has a unique Game ID, including game rules, game content, and the maximum number of players allowed. This table is used to define the rules and configurations of the game, ensuring the rationality of the game battles.

Record the game records of a single player. Each record includes Player ID, Game ID, game start time, game end time, and game status. This table supports the recording and querying of single-player games, tracking the player's status in each game.

4. Player Communication Management
Record the communication content between players. Each record includes the first Player ID, second Player ID, communication start time, communication end time, and communication content. This table is used to save the chat records or command content between players during game battles.

5. Two-Player Battle Game Management
Record the battle information between two players. Each record includes the first Player ID, second Player ID, Game ID, battle start time, battle end time, and battle results. This table manages two-player battle games, recording the operations and results of the battling players.

CREATE TABLE `student` (
  `student_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `telephone` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `email` varchar(255) NOT NULL,

  `name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `telephone` varchar(255) NOT NULL,

Quartz is an open-source job scheduling framework widely used in Java applications, responsible for managing and scheduling timed tasks. The system supports task definition, trigger management, Cron scheduling, simple triggers, task instance management, and other functions. 

The core entities in the system include tasks, schedulers, triggers, and locks. The task entity mainly consists of task ID, task name, task description, class name, persistence flag, and concurrent execution flag. The task ID is the unique identifier, and all other properties depend on the task ID. The scheduler entity contains scheduler ID, scheduler name, scheduler status, scheduler configuration, and scheduler logs, with the scheduler ID being the unique identifier, and other Attributes describing the configuration and status of the scheduler. The trigger entity includes trigger ID and trigger name, recording basic information for all triggers in the system. Additionally, triggers are divided into sub-entities by type, such as simple triggers, Cron triggers, complex triggers, and Blob triggers, each type having different Attributes.

Simple triggers include trigger ID, trigger name, trigger type, repeat count, repeat interval, and triggered count; Cron triggers contain trigger ID, trigger name, trigger type, Cron expression, and timezone; complex triggers include trigger ID, trigger name, trigger type, and Attributes like string, integer, long integer, decimal, and boolean; Blob triggers possess trigger ID, trigger name, trigger type, and binary Attributes. The lock entity is used to control concurrency in the task scheduling process, with Attributes including lock ID, lock name, lock status, and lock description.

The relationships within the system are also crucial. The task-to-trigger relationship table records the association between each task and its triggers, containing task ID, trigger ID, next execution time, last execution time, priority, trigger status, start time, end time, calendar name, and fault instruction. Each task can use multiple triggers, and each trigger may also be associated with multiple tasks. The scheduler-to-task relationship table describes which schedulers schedule which tasks, linking scheduler ID, task ID, and trigger ID. The scheduler-to-lock relationship table records the relationship between schedulers and locks, ensuring lock management in a multi-instance environment, Attributes include scheduler ID, lock ID, acquisition time, and release time. 

These entities and relationships constitute the basic framework of the task scheduling system, ensuring task scheduling, execution, and concurrency control, adapting to complex scheduling requirements and multi-instance environments.

Vehicle Management: The system records detailed information for vehicles, including Vehicle Identification Number (VIN), manufacturer, model, year, and driver information. Each vehicle is identified by a unique VIN, and the system supports assigning personnel as drivers for vehicles. Drivers are linked to the Personnel table by a Foreign key to the ID and are updated through cascading updates.

Insurance Management: The system records insurance information for each vehicle, detailing each vehicle's purchased insurance and the specifics of the insurance (Insurance Type ID, Insurance Company Name, Insurance Cost, Insurance Content), along with the specific time of purchase and the validity period of the insurance for the vehicle.

Phone Management: The system allows recording multiple phone numbers for each personnel. Each phone number is associated with personnel via ID and uniquely identified by a composite Primary key of ID and Number. Each phone number's information includes: ID (Foreign key) and Number (phone number).

CREATE TABLE Personnel (
    City VARCHAR(255),
    Name VARCHAR(255),
    Personnel_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Street VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Insurance_Type (
    Insurance_Company_Name VARCHAR(255),
    Insurance_Content VARCHAR(255),
    Insurance_Cost FLOAT,
    Insurance_Type_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY
);

CREATE TABLE Vehicle (
    Driver_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Manufacturer VARCHAR(255),
    Model VARCHAR(255),
    Vin VARCHAR(255) PRIMARY KEY,
    Year INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (Driver_ID) REFERENCES Personnel(Personnel_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE User_Phone_Table (
    Phone_Number INTEGER,
    User_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (User_ID, Phone_Number),
    FOREIGN KEY (User_ID) REFERENCES Personnel(Personnel_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Vehicle_Purchase_Insurance (
    Insurance_Type_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Purchase_Time DATETIME,
    Validity_Time DATETIME,
    Vin VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Vin, Insurance_Type_ID, Purchase_Time),
    FOREIGN KEY (Insurance_Type_ID) REFERENCES Insurance_Type(Insurance_Type_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Vin) REFERENCES Vehicle(Vin)
);

Business Requirements Description:
This system is designed for managing and monitoring web services in various applications. Key requirements include:
Each user has a unique username, email, and role. User roles are associated with specific permissions. Users can be assigned different roles and permissions that are linked to particular applications.
Each application has a unique ID, code, name, and type.
Each web service has a unique ID, name, description, and creation date. It records error information, including error codes, descriptions, timestamps, and return status.
Monitors the invocation of web services, recording details like invocation time, return status, delay time, and other performance metrics.
Tracks statistics such as success rate and call count over a specific time period.
Tracks which users are authorized to access which applications.
Links error data with monitoring data to enable detailed analysis and reporting.
hyp_nl: The database schema named 'rschema_0344' consists of 8 tables. The 'User' table is used to store user information, including the user's email, unique identifier, and username. The 'Application' table stores information about the applications, including the application's unique identifier, code, name, and type. The 'Web_Service' table contains information about web services, including the unique identifier of the application they belong to, creation date, description, name, and the unique identifier of the service itself. The 'Permissions' table stores information about the permissions of users on different applications, including the unique identifiers of the application and user, and the role. The 'Error_Information' table stores information about errors, including the unique identifier of the error, error code, description, occurrence time, return status, and the unique identifier of the service it belongs to. The 'Service_Monitoring' table stores information about service monitoring, including the call time, delay time, unique identifier of the monitoring, return status, and the unique identifier of the service. The 'Statistics' table stores statistics about services, including the call count, success rate, time period, and the unique identifier of the service. Finally, the 'Error_and_Monitoring_Association' table is used to associate errors with their corresponding monitoring records, using the unique identifiers of the error and monitoring records. CREATE TABLE User (
    email VARCHAR(255),
    user_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    username VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Application (
    application_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    code VARCHAR(255),
    name VARCHAR(255),
    type VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Web_Service (
    application_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    creation_date DATETIME,
    description VARCHAR(255),
    name VARCHAR(255),
    service_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    FOREIGN KEY (application_ID) REFERENCES Application(application_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Permissions (
    application_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    permission_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    role VARCHAR(255),
    user_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (application_ID) REFERENCES Application(application_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (user_ID) REFERENCES User(user_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Error_Information (
    error_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    error_code VARCHAR(255),
    error_description VARCHAR(255),
    occurrence_time DATETIME,
    return_status VARCHAR(255),
    service_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (service_ID) REFERENCES Web_Service(service_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Service_Monitoring (
    call_time DATETIME,
    delay_time DATETIME,
    monitoring_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    return_status VARCHAR(255),
    service_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (service_ID) REFERENCES Web_Service(service_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Statistics (
    call_count INTEGER,
    service_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    statistic_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    success_rate FLOAT,
    time_period DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY (service_ID) REFERENCES Web_Service(service_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Error_and_Monitoring_Association (
    error_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    monitoring_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (error_ID) REFERENCES Error_Information(error_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (monitoring_ID) REFERENCES Service_Monitoring(monitoring_ID)
);

A machine learning model management and evaluation system is used to record and manage the operational status, performance metrics, hyperparameter settings, and dataset information of various machine learning models. The requirements analysis is as follows:
Model Run Records: Records the run ID, execution time, start time, end time, runtime, run path, maximum number of models, and model types for each model, implemented through the Leaderboard_Metadata table.
Model Performance Evaluation: Records the ID, name, performance metrics (such as RMSE, MSE, MAE, RMSLE), and whether the best family model of stacked ensemble exists for each model, implemented through the Leaderboard table.
Hyperparameter Management: Records the ID and name of hyperparameters, implemented through the Hyperparameter table, and records the hyperparameter values for each model, implemented through the Hyperparameter_Values table.
Model-Run Association: Records the association between each model and its run, implemented through the Model_Run table.
Dataset Management: Records the ID, name, owner, license, visibility, URL, creation date, last update date, data size, number of rows, and number of columns for each dataset, implemented through the Dataset_Metadata table.
Dataset-Run Association: Records the association between each dataset and its run, implemented through the Data_Map table.
Model Type Management: Records the ID and name of model types, implemented through the Model_Map table.
Hyperparameter Default Value Management: Records the default hyperparameter values for each model type, implemented through the Hyperparameter_Def_Values table.
Model Type-Model Association: Records the type of each model, implemented through the ID_Map table.
Dataset Variable Details: Records the ID, name, data type, number of unique values, and number of null values for each variable in the dataset, implemented through the Dataset_Variable_Details table, with each dataset's detailed information linked to a dataset.
Dataset Tag Management: Records the ID and name of dataset tags, implemented through the Tags table, and records the association between each dataset and its tags, implemented through the Tag_Map table.

The 'leaderboard_metadata' table holds metadata about the model runs, including the execution time, start and end times, run time, run path, maximum models, and model species. The primary key is 'run_id'.
The 'leaderboard' table represents the leaderboard, storing information about each model, including the model id, model name, and various metrics such as root mean squared error (RMSE), mean squared error (MSE), mean absolute error (MAE), root mean squared log error (RMSLE), and the presence of stacked ensemble best of family. The primary key is 'model_id'.
The 'model_map' table maps model types to their corresponding ids and names. The primary key is 'model_type_id'.
The 'dataset_variable_details' table holds information about the variables in the datasets, including the variable id, name of variables, data type of variable, unique values in each column, null values in each column, and the dataset id. The 'hyperparameter_value' table holds the values of hyperparameters for each model, including the model id, hyperparameter id, and the value. The primary key is a combination of 'hyperparameter_id' and 'model_id', and foreign keys 'hyperparameter_id' and 'model_id' reference 'hyperparameter' and 'leaderboard' tables respectively.
The 'model_run' table maps model runs to their corresponding model ids and run ids. The primary key is a combination of 'model_id' and 'run_id', and foreign keys 'model_id' and 'run_id' reference 'leaderboard' and 'leaderboard_metadata' tables respectively.
The 'data_map' table maps datasets to their corresponding run ids. The primary key is a combination of 'dataset_id' and 'run_id', and foreign keys 'dataset_id' and 'run_id' reference 'dataset_metadata' and 'leaderboard_metadata' tables respectively.
The 'hyperparameter_def_values' table holds default values for hyperparameters for each model type. The primary key is a combination of 'model_type_id' and 'hyperparameter_id', and foreign keys 'hyperparameter_id' and 'model_type_id' reference 'hyperparameter' and 'model_map' tables respectively.
The 'id_map' table maps model ids to their corresponding model type ids. The primary key is 'model_id', and foreign key 'model_id' references 'leaderboard' table, while foreign key 'model_type_id' references 'model_map' table.

-- Schema for database: rschema_0347

CREATE TABLE `leaderboard_metadata` (
  `run_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `model_execution_time` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `start_time` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `end_time` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `run_time` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `run_path` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `max_models` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `model_species` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`run_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `leaderboard` (
  `model_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `model_name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `rmse` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `mse` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `mae` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `rmsle` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `presence_stackedensembled_best_of_family` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`model_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `model_map` (
  `model_type_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `model_type_name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`model_type_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `dataset_variable_details` (
  `var_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `name_of_variables` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `datatype_of_variable` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `unique_values_in_each_column` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `null_values_in_each_column` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `dataset_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`var_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `dataset_variable_details_ibfk_dataset_id` FOREIGN KEY (`dataset_id`) REFERENCES `dataset_metadata` (`dataset_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `tags` (
  `tag_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `tag_name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`tag_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `hyperparameter_value` (
  `model_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `hyperparameter_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `value` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`hyperparameter_id`, `model_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `hyperparameter_value_ibfk_hyperparameter_id` FOREIGN KEY (`hyperparameter_id`) REFERENCES `hyperparameter` (`hyperparameter_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `hyperparameter_value_ibfk_model_id` FOREIGN KEY (`model_id`) REFERENCES `leaderboard` (`model_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `model_run` (
  `run_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `model_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`model_id`, `run_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `model_run_ibfk_model_id` FOREIGN KEY (`model_id`) REFERENCES `leaderboard` (`model_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `model_run_ibfk_run_id` FOREIGN KEY (`run_id`) REFERENCES `leaderboard_metadata` (`run_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `data_map` (
  `dataset_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `run_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`dataset_id`, `run_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `data_map_ibfk_dataset_id` FOREIGN KEY (`dataset_id`) REFERENCES `dataset_metadata` (`dataset_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `data_map_ibfk_run_id` FOREIGN KEY (`run_id`) REFERENCES `leaderboard_metadata` (`run_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `hyperparameter_def_values` (
  `model_type_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `hyperparameter_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `default_value` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`model_type_id`, `hyperparameter_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `hyperparameter_def_values_ibfk_hyperparameter_id` FOREIGN KEY (`hyperparameter_id`) REFERENCES `hyperparameter` (`hyperparameter_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `hyperparameter_def_values_ibfk_model_type_id` FOREIGN KEY (`model_type_id`) REFERENCES `model_map` (`model_type_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `id_map` (
  `model_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `model_type_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`model_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `id_map_ibfk_model_id` FOREIGN KEY (`model_id`) REFERENCES `leaderboard` (`model_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `id_map_ibfk_model_type_id` FOREIGN KEY (`model_type_id`) REFERENCES `model_map` (`model_type_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `hyperparameter` (
  `hyperparameter_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`hyperparameter_id`)

CREATE TABLE `dataset_metadata` (
  `dataset_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,

  `licence` varchar(255) NOT NULL,

  `number_of_rows` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `number_of_columns` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`dataset_id`)

CREATE TABLE Maze (

    Maze_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Maze_Name VARCHAR(255)
);

    Contact_Information VARCHAR(255),
    Name VARCHAR(255),
    User_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY
);

    Maze_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Robot_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Robot_Type VARCHAR(255),
    Timer_Status VARCHAR(255),
    FOREIGN KEY (Maze_ID) REFERENCES Maze(Maze_ID)
);

    Left_Status VARCHAR(255),
    Right_Status VARCHAR(255),

);

    Ghost_Status VARCHAR(255),
    Robot_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Sensor_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,

);

CREATE TABLE Timer (
    Robot_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Timer_Event_Description VARCHAR(255),
    Timer_Event_Time DATETIME,
    Timer_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    FOREIGN KEY (Robot_ID) REFERENCES Robot(Robot_ID)
);
